g.text: SKILL 5 OF 5 · §2.5 PAPER2REEL
Paper2Reel is a presentation surface, not a fourth summary: one alignment
sidecar makes four artifacts views of one section
Figure 9: hover highlights a section; double-click opens video, captions, thumbnails, and the aligned blog passage
FIG. 9
INTERACTION DESIGN
Poster-first: the first screen is the generated poster, not a
dashboard
Hover feedback; double-click opens the section modal — video left,
blog right, draggable splitter
Playback uses the subtitle-free source; captions come from
sidecars behind the viewer's toggle
Slide thumbnails seek to their time; the title area opens a full-paper
modal; EN / 中文 switch in the header
CONTENT ALIGNMENT
The alignment sidecar maps each canonical section id to its poster block, one or more slide targets,
video start and end, subtitle tracks, thumbnails, and blog blocks; the viewer never scrapes filenames,
the poster, or the video
On a PDF, an arXiv link, or a partial bundle, missing upstream stages are completed through the full
workflows, preserving section ids and asset paths
Root: the viewer page, the alignment record, the manifest; poster, media, slides, blog, and downloads in
their own folders; native files stay downloadable
VALIDATED AS AN INTERACTIVE ARTIFACT
Static gate: viewer, alignment record, manifest, copied poster assets, media, slide frames, blog blocks,
wordmark, downloads all present; no stale tabbed-viewer markers, machine-local paths, or backup files; raw
pre-subtitle video as playback source
Browser gate: served with a range-capable local server (seeking and thumbnail jumps need partial-content
responses); headless checks of poster-first load, hover, both modals, split pane, subtitle toggle, thumbnail
and direct seeking, menu, downloads, shortcuts, blog rendering
A separate file-browser gate confirms the page also opens directly from disk
Bundle root, kept to three files
The interactive viewer page, the alignment record, and the
package manifest; poster, media, slides, blog, and downloads sit
in their own folders and stay downloadable as native files.
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)
